comment: Rotula ZPL command catalogue. Edit this file, then run tools/gen-zpl-coverage to refresh docs/zpl-coverage.md. Tests check it against the real parser and generator.

commands.name: Change the command prefix
commands.summary: Replaces the caret that starts every command with another character.
commands.notes: Files that change the prefix are misread from that point on, because Rotula always looks for the default characters. The command is kept, but what follows it is not understood.

commands.name: Change the delimiter
commands.summary: Replaces the comma that separates command parameters with another character.
commands.notes: Files that change the delimiter are misread from that point on: parameters are always split at commas.

commands.name: Change the tilde prefix
commands.summary: Replaces the tilde that starts the immediate commands with another character.
commands.notes: Files that change it are misread from that point on.

commands.name: Label home
commands.summary: Moves the zero point of all positions by a fixed offset from the top-left corner of the label.

commands.name: Label length
commands.summary: Sets the length of the label in dots.

commands.name: Reverse all fields
commands.summary: Prints every field that follows as white on black or black on white, as if each had its own reverse switch.
commands.notes: Imported as a reverse flag on each field that follows, so the label prints the same; Rotula writes the flag per field, not ^LR.

commands.name: Label shift
commands.summary: Shifts every field to the left by a number of dots; a negative value shifts to the right.
commands.notes: Written only when it is not zero.

commands.name: Label top
commands.summary: Moves the whole format down (or up for a negative value) by a few dot rows to fine-tune where it lands on the label.
commands.notes: Rotula accepts -240 to 240; most printers only accept -120 to 120.

commands.name: Units of measure
commands.summary: Switches the units used by later numbers to dots, inches or millimetres.
commands.notes: Values are converted to dots on import and a notice is shown.

commands.name: Mirror the label
commands.summary: Prints the whole label as a mirror image, left to right.
commands.notes: The Preview window shows it mirrored ("As printed"); the canvas and the image and PDF exports stay as designed.

commands.name: Print orientation
commands.summary: Prints the whole label rotated by 180 degrees.
commands.notes: The Preview window shows it upside down ("As printed", with a switch to "As designed"); the canvas and the image and PDF exports stay upright.

commands.name: Print quantity
commands.summary: Sets how many labels print, how many between pauses, and how many copies of each serial number.

commands.name: Print width
commands.summary: Sets the width of the printable area in dots.

commands.name: Start of label
commands.summary: Opens a label format. Everything up to the matching end-of-label command belongs to one label.

commands.name: End of label
commands.summary: Closes a label format and sends it to print.

commands.name: Field block
commands.summary: Wraps text inside a block of a given width, with line limit, spacing, alignment and hanging indent.
commands.notes: The preview uses a stand-in typeface, so line breaks can differ a little from the printer.

commands.name: Field clock indicators
commands.summary: Chooses the characters that mark real-time-clock codes (date and time) inside a field.
commands.notes: The preview shows the codes as typed, not the date. Works only on printers with a clock. A date variable set to use the printer clock writes this command by itself (see docs/variables.md).

commands.name: Field data
commands.summary: Holds the text or data of a field.

commands.name: Field number embedding character
commands.summary: Chooses the character that marks references to numbered fields inside the data of a field.
commands.notes: The text is written unchanged; the printer expands the references.

commands.name: Hexadecimal escapes in field data
commands.summary: Lets field data carry any byte as an underscore and two hex digits, so accents and control characters survive.
commands.notes: Written automatically whenever the text needs it.

commands.name: Multiple field origins
commands.summary: Gives the places where each part of a PDF417 or MicroPDF417 symbol that is split over several symbols is printed.
commands.notes: A field that uses it is kept whole as raw ZPL.

commands.name: Field number
commands.summary: Gives a field a number so its data can be filled in or reused later; an optional prompt can be stored with it.
commands.notes: Kept on the field and written back. Filling numbered fields from a stored template is not done by Rotula yet.

commands.name: Field origin
commands.summary: Starts a field and places its top-left corner at the given position.

commands.name: Field direction
commands.summary: Prints the characters of a text field top to bottom or right to left, with an optional gap between characters.
commands.notes: Text fields only. The preview always draws left to right.

commands.name: Reverse a field
commands.summary: Prints one field as the opposite of what is already under it.

commands.name: Field separator
commands.summary: Ends a field.

commands.name: Field typeset position
commands.summary: Starts a field and places it by its baseline (text) or bottom-left corner (other objects).

commands.name: Field variable data
commands.summary: Holds the data of a field the same way ^FD does; used in stored formats to mark data that changes.
commands.notes: Read as ^FD and written as ^FD.

commands.name: Default field rotation
commands.summary: Sets the rotation that fields use unless they give their own.

commands.name: Comment
commands.summary: A note for people reading the file; it prints nothing.
commands.notes: Kept as a raw element so notes survive a round trip, without a warning.

commands.name: Serialization mask
commands.summary: Makes the printer change selected characters of the field data on every label, following a mask.
commands.notes: The first label's value is shown.

commands.name: Serial number (counting)
commands.summary: Makes the printer count a number up or down on every label of a print run.
commands.notes: The first label's value is shown. This is separate from the counters of the merge feature, which write a different literal value per record.

commands.name: Text box
commands.summary: Wraps text inside a box of fixed width and height and drops the lines that do not fit.
commands.notes: A less-than sign in the text is written as three characters so the printer does not read it as an escape. Line breaks in the text become spaces.

commands.name: Font selection
commands.summary: Chooses a font, its rotation, and its height and width in dots. A letter or digit picks a built-in or assigned font.
commands.notes: Includes ^A0 (the scalable font) and ^A@ (a font addressed by file name, which is kept with a warning). The preview draws every font with a stand-in typeface.

commands.name: Default font
commands.summary: Sets the font and size used by fields that do not choose their own.

commands.name: Character set
commands.summary: Chooses how the bytes of field data map to characters; Rotula writes UTF-8 by default.
commands.notes: National sets and remapping parameters give a warning.

commands.name: Character cache
commands.summary: Sets the size of the printer's character cache, or the font memory it uses.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Font identifier
commands.summary: Assigns a one-character font id to a font file stored on the printer.
commands.notes: Kept as a document setting and written before the fields. A change after the first field is kept as raw ZPL with a warning.

commands.name: Download bitmap font
commands.summary: Sends a bitmap font to the printer.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim; the data is binary.

commands.name: Download encoding
commands.summary: Sends a character encoding table to the printer.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Download scalable font
commands.summary: Sends a scalable font to the printer.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim; the data is binary.

commands.name: Download TrueType font
commands.summary: Sends a TrueType font to the printer.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim; the data is binary.

commands.name: Download unbounded TrueType font
commands.summary: Sends a TrueType font of any size to the printer.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim; the data is binary.

commands.name: Font linking
commands.summary: Links fonts so characters missing from one are taken from another.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Advanced text properties
commands.summary: Switches on bidirectional text, glyph shaping and similar options for complex scripts.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Box and lines
commands.summary: Draws a rectangle with a border; a box that is as thin as its border is a straight line.

commands.name: Circle
commands.summary: Draws a circle with a border of a chosen thickness.

commands.name: Diagonal line
commands.summary: Draws a straight diagonal line corner to corner across a box, leaning right or left.

commands.name: Ellipse
commands.summary: Draws an ellipse with a border of a chosen thickness.

commands.name: Graphic field
commands.summary: Prints a black-and-white bitmap sent as data inside the field.
commands.notes: Output is ASCII hex. Input also accepts ZPL run-length compression and Z64 or B64 data; the binary formats are kept as raw ZPL.

commands.name: Graphic symbol
commands.summary: Prints a registered, copyright or trademark sign, or the UL or CSA approval mark.
commands.notes: The printer draws the symbol from its own font; the preview shows the nearest letters or signs.

commands.name: Aztec Code (zero spelling)
commands.summary: The guide also lists Aztec Code as ^B0, with a zero. It is read exactly like ^BO.
commands.notes: Read as ^BO and written as ^BO.

commands.name: Code 11
commands.summary: Prints a Code 11 barcode with one or two check digits.

commands.name: Interleaved 2 of 5
commands.summary: Prints a numeric Interleaved 2 of 5 barcode with an optional check digit.

commands.name: Code 39
commands.summary: Prints a Code 39 barcode with an optional check digit.

commands.name: Code 49
commands.summary: Prints a Code 49 stacked barcode.
commands.notes: The printer draws it; the preview shows a labelled box.

commands.name: PLANET Code
commands.summary: Prints a PLANET postal barcode.

commands.name: PDF417
commands.summary: Prints a PDF417 stacked barcode with a chosen security level and size.

commands.name: EAN-8
commands.summary: Prints an EAN-8 product barcode.

commands.name: UPC-E
commands.summary: Prints a UPC-E short product barcode.
commands.notes: The designer also accepts the 6-digit UPC-E form and writes the code the printer expects.

commands.name: Code 93
commands.summary: Prints a Code 93 barcode with an optional check digit.

commands.name: Codablock
commands.summary: Prints a Codablock A, E or F stacked barcode.
commands.notes: The printer draws it; the preview shows a labelled box.

commands.name: Code 128
commands.summary: Prints a Code 128 barcode, a dense code for any text, with optional mode and human-readable line.

commands.name: UPS MaxiCode
commands.summary: Prints a UPS MaxiCode symbol.
commands.notes: The printer draws it; the preview shows a labelled box.

commands.name: EAN-13
commands.summary: Prints an EAN-13 product barcode.

commands.name: MicroPDF417
commands.summary: Prints a MicroPDF417 symbol, the small version of PDF417.
commands.notes: The printer draws it; the preview shows a labelled box.

commands.name: Industrial 2 of 5
commands.summary: Prints an Industrial 2 of 5 numeric barcode.
commands.notes: The guide has no printed sample, so the preview follows the published definition.

commands.name: Standard 2 of 5
commands.summary: Prints a Standard 2 of 5 numeric barcode.

commands.name: ANSI Codabar
commands.summary: Prints a Codabar barcode; the start and stop characters are options, not part of the data.

commands.name: LOGMARS
commands.summary: Prints a LOGMARS barcode, a Code 39 variant with a mandatory check character.
commands.notes: The check character is always added.

commands.name: MSI
commands.summary: Prints an MSI barcode with a choice of check digit schemes.

commands.name: Aztec Code
commands.summary: Prints an Aztec Code with magnification, error control and the menu, rune and structured-append options.
commands.notes: Rune, menu, structured append and ECI symbols are shown as a placeholder in the preview.

commands.name: Plessey
commands.summary: Prints a Plessey barcode.

commands.name: QR Code
commands.summary: Prints a QR Code with a chosen model, size and error correction.
commands.notes: Manual mode gives a warning.

commands.name: GS1 DataBar
commands.summary: Prints a GS1 DataBar symbol of types 1 to 6, including stacked and expanded.
commands.notes: Types 7 to 12 and composite data are kept as raw ZPL with a warning.

commands.name: UPC/EAN add-on
commands.summary: Prints the 2- or 5-digit add-on that sits next to a UPC or EAN barcode.

commands.name: TLC39
commands.summary: Prints a TLC39 symbol, a Code 39 line with a MicroPDF417 part.
commands.notes: The printer draws it; the preview shows a labelled box.

commands.name: UPC-A
commands.summary: Prints a UPC-A product barcode.

commands.name: Data Matrix
commands.summary: Prints a Data Matrix symbol (ECC 200).
commands.notes: Quality below 200 gives a warning.

commands.name: Barcode defaults
commands.summary: Sets the default module width, wide-to-narrow ratio and height used by the barcodes that follow.

commands.name: POSTNET and PLANET
commands.summary: Prints a POSTNET or PLANET postal barcode.
commands.notes: Types 2 and 3 (Intelligent Mail) are kept as raw ZPL with a warning.

commands.name: Code validation
commands.summary: Makes the printer check barcode data and reject bad barcodes.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Store format
commands.summary: Saves the commands that follow as a reusable template in the printer's memory.
commands.notes: Templates, with numbered fields filled in at print time, are planned. Today the command is kept verbatim with a warning.

commands.name: Download graphic
commands.summary: Sends a bitmap to the printer's memory under a name, to be printed later with ^XG or ^IM.
commands.notes: Kept as a document setting and written before the label. A recall in the same file is drawn in the preview.

commands.name: Abort graphic download
commands.reason: A diagnostic or immediate printer action that prints nothing on the label.
commands.summary: Stops a graphic download that is in progress.

commands.name: Download object
commands.summary: Sends a file (a bitmap, font or other object) to the printer's memory.
commands.notes: Only plain bitmap data (hex or Z64 text, format A, type G or B) is understood; it is written back as ~DG. PNG, TrueType and binary downloads are kept as raw ZPL.

commands.name: Erase all graphics
commands.summary: Deletes every stored graphic from the printer's memory.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Delete stored object
commands.summary: Deletes objects from the printer's memory.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Image load
commands.summary: Loads a stored label image at the top-left corner as the background of the label.
commands.notes: Kept as a stored-object placeholder.

commands.name: Image move
commands.summary: Prints a graphic stored on the printer at its original size.
commands.notes: Kept as a stored-object placeholder. When the same file downloads the graphic with ~DG, the preview draws it.

commands.name: Image save
commands.summary: Saves the label format as an image in the printer's memory instead of printing it.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim with a warning.

commands.name: Transfer object
commands.reason: Manages the printer's own storage; it does not change what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Copies stored objects from one storage device to another.

commands.name: Recall format
commands.summary: Prints a stored template, filling its numbered fields.
commands.notes: Planned together with ^DF. Today the recall is kept as a stored-object placeholder with a warning.

commands.name: Recall graphic
commands.summary: Prints a graphic stored on the printer, at a chosen magnification.
commands.notes: Kept as a stored-object placeholder. When the same file downloads the graphic with ~DG, the preview draws it.

commands.name: Calibrate media sensor
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Starts media calibration.

commands.name: Start communications diagnostics
commands.reason: A diagnostic or immediate printer action that prints nothing on the label.
commands.summary: Switches communications diagnostics on.

commands.name: Stop communications diagnostics
commands.reason: A diagnostic or immediate printer action that prints nothing on the label.
commands.summary: Switches communications diagnostics off.

commands.name: Graph the sensor
commands.reason: A diagnostic or immediate printer action that prints nothing on the label.
commands.summary: Prints a graph of the sensor readings.

commands.name: Dots per millimetre
commands.summary: Switches the printer to half its resolution for large labels.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim. Rotula keeps the resolution you chose for the label.

commands.name: Sensor select
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Chooses which sensor tracks the media.

commands.name: Backfeed sequence
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Changes when the printer backs the media up.

commands.name: Ribbon tension
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets how tight the ribbon is held.

commands.name: Reprint after error
commands.summary: Chooses whether the label is reprinted after a media or ribbon error.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Media darkness
commands.summary: Makes the print lighter or darker relative to the printer's current darkness.
commands.notes: Decimal values are allowed.

commands.name: Media feed at power-up and head close
commands.summary: Chooses whether the printer feeds, calibrates or does nothing when it starts or the printhead closes.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Maximum label length
commands.summary: Tells the printer the longest label it may have to measure during calibration.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Print mode
commands.summary: Chooses what the printer does after printing: tear-off, peel, rewind, applicator, cutter, delayed cutter, RFID or kiosk.
commands.notes: The reserved modes L and U are kept as raw ZPL with a warning.

commands.name: Media tracking
commands.summary: Tells the printer how to find the start of each label: continuous, gap or mark.

commands.name: Media type
commands.summary: Chooses thermal transfer (ribbon) or direct thermal media.

commands.name: Slew dot rows
commands.summary: Feeds blank dot rows before the label prints.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Slew to home
commands.summary: Feeds the media to the start of the next label.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim. The ~ form does the same as an immediate command.

commands.name: Programmable pause
commands.summary: Pauses the printer after the label so the operator has to confirm.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim. The ~ form pauses at once.

commands.name: Print rate
commands.summary: Sets the print, slew and backfeed speeds.
commands.notes: Speeds are written as inches per second (1 to 14); the letters A to E are read as 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8.

commands.name: Applicator reprint
commands.reason: Controls kiosk or presenter hardware; it is not part of the label artwork.
commands.summary: Reprints the last label on an applicator.

commands.name: Resume printing
commands.reason: A diagnostic or immediate printer action that prints nothing on the label.
commands.summary: Restarts a printer that is paused.

commands.name: Set darkness
commands.summary: Sets the print darkness to an absolute level from 0 to 30.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Set sensor intensity
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets how strongly the media sensors shine.

commands.name: Start print early
commands.summary: Starts printing while the rest of the label is still being formatted.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Set media sensors
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets the values the media sensors use.

commands.name: Tear-off adjust
commands.summary: Moves the position where labels stop for tearing off.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Suppress backfeed
commands.summary: Stops the printer from backing the media up after cutting or peeling.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Memory letter assignment
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Changes which letters name the memory devices.

commands.name: Cancel all
commands.reason: A diagnostic or immediate printer action that prints nothing on the label.
commands.summary: Cancels every format waiting in the printer.

commands.name: Initialize flash memory
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Erases a flash memory device.

commands.name: Reset optional memory
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Erases the optional memory card.

commands.name: Battery condition
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets the battery condition setting.

commands.name: Early warning settings
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets which early warnings the printer gives.

commands.name: Start ZBI program
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Starts a Zebra Basic Interpreter program.

commands.name: Auxiliary port
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets how the auxiliary port is used.

commands.name: Set label length
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Makes the printer measure the label length.

commands.name: Head test fatal
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Makes a failed printhead test stop the printer.

commands.name: Head test non-fatal
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Makes a failed printhead test only warn.

commands.name: Pause and cancel format
commands.reason: A diagnostic or immediate printer action that prints nothing on the label.
commands.summary: Pauses the printer and cancels the current format.

commands.name: Terminate ZBI
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Stops a running Zebra Basic Interpreter program.

commands.name: Power-on reset
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Restarts the printer.

commands.name: Printhead test interval
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets how often the printhead is tested.

commands.name: Configuration update
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Saves or restores the printer settings.

commands.name: Cancel partial format
commands.reason: A diagnostic or immediate printer action that prints nothing on the label.
commands.summary: Cancels a format that is only partly received.

commands.name: Kill battery
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Switches the printer's battery off.

commands.name: Date and time format
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Chooses how the printer shows the date and time.

commands.name: Define language
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets the language of the printer's own display.

commands.name: Printer name
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets the printer's name and description.

commands.name: Set password
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets the printer's panel password.

commands.name: Maintenance alerts
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets when the printer prints maintenance warnings.

commands.name: Map clear
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Chooses whether the format memory is cleared after printing.

commands.name: Maintenance information message
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets the text of maintenance messages.

commands.name: Mode protection
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Locks printer modes against changes from the panel.

commands.name: Printhead cold warning
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Switches the cold printhead warning on or off.

commands.name: Decommissioning mode
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Wipes the printer's memory before it is retired.

commands.name: Reset advanced counters
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Resets the printer's usage counters.

commands.name: Serial communications
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets the serial port speed and format.

commands.name: Encoding table
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Chooses the encoding table the printer uses.

commands.name: Clock mode and language
commands.summary: Sets the format and language the printer uses for date and time codes in fields.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim.

commands.name: Clock offset
commands.summary: Sets an offset added to the real-time clock for date and time codes.
commands.notes: Kept verbatim when imported. Rotula also writes it by itself for date variables that use the printer clock with an offset (see docs/variables.md); that copy is not read back into the model.

commands.name: Printhead resistance
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets the printhead resistance value.

commands.name: Set date and time
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Sets the printer's real-time clock.

commands.name: ZPL mode
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Chooses between ZPL and ZPL II.

commands.name: Dynamic media calibration
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Switches dynamic media calibration on or off.

commands.name: Printer sleep
commands.reason: Printer administration: it changes how the device is set up, not what a label looks like.
commands.summary: Puts the printer to sleep after a time.

commands.name: Battery status
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Asks a mobile printer for its battery status.

commands.name: Head diagnostic
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Asks for printhead diagnostics.

commands.name: Host format
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Sends a stored format back to the host.

commands.name: Host graphic
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Sends a stored graphic back to the host.

commands.name: Configuration label return
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Sends the printer configuration back to the host.

commands.name: Host identification
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Asks the printer to identify itself.

commands.name: Host RAM status
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Asks for the memory status.

commands.name: Host query
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Asks for a named piece of printer information.

commands.name: Host status
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply. Rotula's printing sends it on its own to check the printer before a job and to verify the job afterwards (see docs/printing.md).
commands.summary: Asks for the printer status.

commands.name: Host linked fonts list
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Asks for the list of linked fonts.

commands.name: Alert configuration return
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Sends the alert configuration back to the host.

commands.name: Host verification
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
commands.summary: Sends the data of a field back to the host.

commands.name: Host directory list
commands.reason: A query that makes the printer answer the host; a label file has no use for the reply.
